From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: MAP Draft: POC Environment & Network/Identity Dependencies

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is the first draft of the Mutual Action Plan (POC_MAP_v1.xlsx). Below is a concise recap of the POC milestone we agreed to prioritize and the current suggested owners/target dates. Please review and confirm or flag changes.

High-level POC milestone: Stand up a private POC environment with Redwood inference runtime reachable from Heimdall test VPC, validate basic generation throughput and SSO-protected demo flows. Target POC start: 2026-04-01.

Milestone 1 — Network connectivity: VPC peering or equivalent
- Owner: Heimdall NetOps (coord.) / Redwood infra (acceptor)
- Target: Peering established & routing tested by 2026-03-24
- Dependencies: CIDR confirmation, peering window, security approval
- Blockers: overlapping CIDRs, procurement windows

Milestone 2 — IP allowlists / egress IPs
- Owner: Heimdall Sec / NetOps (apply lists)
- Target: 2026-03-24 (aligned with peering)
- Dependencies: static egress IP list from Redwood (see network-config-template.json)

Milestone 3 — Identity & access (SSO / SAML)
- Owner: Heimdall IAM (IdP) / Redwood SSO team (SP)
- Target: Exchange metadata & smoke test by 2026-03-30
- Dependencies: SAML metadata exchange, test user account

Milestone 4 — Secrets & KMS access
- Owner: Heimdall Security (customer-managed KMS) / Redwood infra (access configuration)
- Target: 2026-03-29
- Dependencies: KMS key ARN, cross-account access policy or delegated role

Milestone 5 — Test data, validation, and success criteria
- Owner: Heimdall Product + Redwood Solutions
- Target: POC validation checklist complete by 2026-04-06

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm owners above and any date changes by EOD 2026-03-13.
2) Technical kickoff with Heimdall NetOps + Redwood infra (please include your NetOps address) — propose 60-min slot week of 2026-03-22.
3) Exchange SAML SP metadata (attached) and sample CIDRs; we will provide static egress IPs and the network template.

Attachments included: POC_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP draft), network-config-template.json, SAML_SP_Metadata.xml

If that looks good I will lock the dates and send a calendar invite for the kickoff.

Thanks,

- Timeline: Procurement & our security review may push some items a week later; can we keep the target POC start flexible to Apr 1-8?
- VPC peering: NetOps asked whether Redwood supports either classic VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink — PrivateLink is preferred for our regulated environment. If peering is required, we will need the desired CIDRs and a peering window (preferably during our maintenance window 03/24 00:00 - 06:00 UTC).
- IP allowlists: please provide your static egress IP addresses and FQDNs (if any). We will only allow a short list — how many IPs should we expect?
- SAML / IdP: We will need your SP metadata and a short list of attributes (email, name, groups). If you need us to create a service account or cross-account role for API access to pull secrets, confirm what you require.
- KMS / Secrets: We use a customer-managed KMS; our security team will expect an access pattern doc and an IAM policy. Can Redwood support KMS key policy + cross-account role?

I've attached our internal network requirements sheet (heimdall-net-requirements.xlsx) for your infra team.

Also looping in NetOps: netops@heimdallcyber.com for scheduling.

Subject: Re: MAP Draft: POC Environment & Network/Identity Dependencies

Alex — thanks for the notes and the sheet. Quick technical clarifications from Redwood infra/solutions side (keeps things actionable):

1) Connectivity options:
- Redwood supports either VPC peering or PrivateLink. PrivateLink is preferred for regulated customers and avoids route table changes on your side. If you choose PrivateLink we will provide the endpoint service name.
- If you prefer VPC peering, we can accept peering requests; please confirm your peering CIDR and a proposed peering window. Suggested peering window: 2026-03-24 00:00 - 06:00 UTC.

2) Egress IPs / allowlist:
- For the POC we will provide a small set of static egress IPs (typically 3–8 IPs depending on region). We'll send the exact list by EOD 2026-03-13.
- If you require FQDNs instead, we can provide TLS hostnames for the API endpoints.

3) SAML / SSO:
- Attached is our SP metadata (SAML_SP_Metadata.xml) and we support HTTP-Redirect/POST bindings. Required attributes: email, givenName, familyName, groups (optional).
- We can support either IdP-initiated or SP-initiated flows. For vault/secrets access we typically create a service account in the customer org and request an IAM role (cross-account) or a short-lived token—either works, we'll align with your security preference.

4) Secrets & KMS:
- Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys. We will need the key ARN and a cross-account policy granting Redwood the decrypt/encrypt permissions, or we can use a delegated role that Redwood assumes. Security documentation: we will share the access pattern doc and a sample IAM policy in the kickoff.

5) Next steps / proposed owners/dates (updated):
- NetOps kickoff: schedule week of 2026-03-22 (owner: Heimdall NetOps + Redwood infra)
- Provide egress IPs (owner: Redwood) by 2026-03-13
- Exchange SP metadata + attributes (owner: Heimdall IAM + Redwood) by 2026-03-18
- KMS access policy agreed (owner: Heimdall Sec + Redwood) by 2026-03-25

I will also prepare a short runbook for the kickoff with the exact commands and test steps for the NetOps run-through. If you confirm the 03/24 window for peering or prefer PrivateLink, we will reserve infra resources accordingly.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min tech call tomorrow if helpful (timeslots: 10:00–12:00 PT).

Best,

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
